leading_positions.synthesis: Six of the eight round-1 files put optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) in their preferred configuration, and all six name the same two laureates. They share the case: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice removes Doppler and recoil shifts, Ye's strontium systems reach 10^-18, independent laboratories agree, and the redefinition of the second is on a roadmap. Citation wording differs in emphasis (invention and development, realisation, magic-wavelength trapping, a new regime of precision measurement). Johansson moved to this position from her own opening first choice, B003, and Pearce moved it above B027. What is not shared: how much weight the 1989, 2005 and 2012 precedents should carry, and whether two names are fair given Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley and others outside the credited list. Danielsson and Eriksson do not prefer B001 but list it as an alternative; Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce list B017 as an alternative.

Two files prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, and both cite the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction followed by the 2018 correlated-insulator and superconductivity experiments as a clean theory-to-experiment pairing with a large downstream field. Both citations pair the flat-band prediction with the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, and both list B001 as an alternative. Both concede that the field is about eight years old, that the pairing mechanism is unsettled, and that Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby, Efetov and others are outside the credited names. They separate the existence of the correlated platform from the unsettled mechanism of superconductivity; Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson list B017 only as an alternative and cite maturity or attribution, and Mehlig and Olsson say it may be stronger in a few years or in a year or two.

One file proposes a two-part prize: the lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) plus IceCube and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos (Halzen alone), three laureates in total. The proposer states that B001 alone would be cleaner and that B027 would be dropped if colleagues find the single-name attribution unconvincing. No other file prefers B027. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig and Olsson each say in round 1 that they would keep B027 for a later year, not this year's lead, and Lindroth shares the attribution and source-significance reservations while deferring to astroparticle colleagues. The shared grounds are a one-name credit for a collaboration-scale project and source identifications at moderate significance.

areas_of_agreement: Optical lattice clocks are described as a scientifically secure result confirmed independently at JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB and SYRTE at the 10^-18 level, and the Katori-Ye pairing is the shortlist configuration for which supporters report the smallest attribution gap; Danielsson and Eriksson do not prefer it but list B001 as an alternative, and Eriksson grants that it is cleaner on attribution.

Several members distinguish the lattice clock from the 2005 frequency-comb prize (comb as readout tool, lattice clock as a separate problem of interrogating many neutral atoms), and Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson treat the overlap as a presentational matter that the citation should address, not a bar.

Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is acknowledged by every member who discusses it as an important theory-to-experiment case; the disagreement concerns timing and attribution, not the quality of the physics.
A single-name IceCube credit is regarded as exposed on attribution by its proposer and by every other member who addresses B027, and several consider it a candidate for a later year.

Circuit QED (B003) is not preferred by any member in round 1; Johansson, who ranked it first at the opening, has moved to B001, and Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce cite the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits as a timing concern.

B015 (tunnel magnetoresistance) is in no preferred configuration; Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson note unresolved credit among Miyazaki, Moodera, Parkin and the Yuasa group, plus the overlap with the 2007 GMR prize.
Members agree that the three-person limit cannot reflect every contributor on B017, B010 and B042 and that the committee should say so openly.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a distinct step beyond the 1989, 2005 and 2012 prizes (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson say yes, though Kroll, Mehlig and Johansson record the overlap as a reservation; Danielsson says he cannot judge from outside the field) or a further prize for precision spectroscopy.

Whether an unsettled pairing mechanism in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene bears on the merit of the discovery (Danielsson and Eriksson say no, comparing high-temperature superconductivity) or on whether the field has stabilised (Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Johansson).
Whether the IceCube diffuse flux alone supports a prize, or whether the case depends on source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) that other members describe as at moderate significance.

Whether the practical payoffs of the clocks (redefinition of the second, constraints on constants, dark-sector searches) are required for timing or only supporting context, as Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson ask.

Whether the clocks should be weighed as a discovery of a new regime of matter, which Eriksson prefers in B017, or as an instrument-driven invention with a new measurement capability, as Kroll, Olsson and Pearce argue.
attribution_disputes: B001: the two credited names are accepted by all six supporters, but Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley and ion-clock contributors are outside the list, and Mehlig and Olsson ask how the citation should weigh Katori's concept against Ye's record-accuracy systems and his earlier comb heritage.

B017: the three credited names are the same in every proposal, but Yuan Cao as first author of the 2018 experiments, plus Dean, Young, Kim, Yacoby and Efetov, are outside them. Danielsson proposes that the committee say openly that experimental credit goes to the group through its leader; Eriksson calls that defensible but open to criticism.
B027: Halzen alone is credited for a collaboration-scale project, with early proposers, detector builders and analysts outside the list.

B010: opening proposals differ (Kane with Mele and Molenkamp, or with Molenkamp and Hasan), the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is uncredited, and Mehlig calls the allocation too unstable for this year while Johansson calls its attribution the least stable on the table.

B042 and B032: Cirac and Zoller appear in both, and the theory versus experiment split among the five B042 names is unresolved; opening proposals were Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger in most files and Bloch, Greiner and Zoller in Mehlig's.

B002 and B003: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are detector leaders and not analysts of the discovery (Pearce notes that Gianotti, Incandela and Heuer could be argued), and Blais versus Girvin cannot be settled with a three-person limit.
maturity_disputes: B017: about eight years since the 2018 experiments, with a pairing mechanism still debated; Danielsson and Eriksson regard this as a normal horizon, while Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson cite maturity as a reservation.
B027: Pearce notes the committee could reasonably call neutrino astronomy a few years short of a prize, since the source associations are statistically less secure than the diffuse flux.
B001: the redefinition of the second has not yet happened, and Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson ask whether it should affect timing or whether demonstrated 10^-18 performance is sufficient.

B003: timing relative to the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits is a concern raised by Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce, and Johansson accepts it against her own opening ballot.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs WACQT and works in circuit and waveguide QED, the area of B003 (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Girvin), and notes that Chalmers hosted researchers connected with the 2025 prize; she discloses subject-matter proximity and defers to the chair on recusal if B003 is taken up. She no longer prefers B003 in round 1.

Kroll reports a doctoral research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder and notes that Jun Ye's work grows out of the JILA comb and laser-stabilisation tradition; no direct tie to Katori or Ye is documented, but he flags it for the committee's recusal judgement on B001.
Lindroth discloses field proximity to the atomic-physics candidates (B001, B032, B042) and asks that it be discounted accordingly; no documented collaborator is a credited name.

Pearce (chair) works in astroparticle physics and discloses professional proximity to B027; his documented collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) do not include IceCube, and he has no recorded tie to Halzen, Katori or Ye.

Eriksson notes research adjacency to B017, B015 and B012 (electronic structure, DFT, magnetism) and Olsson notes oxide-interface work adjacent to B017 and a listed Chalmers connection to Johansson; neither reports a tie to a credited person.
questions_for_round2: For B001, should the citation be worded around the lattice clock and its magic-wavelength concept so that it is distinct from the 2005 comb prize, and does any member regard the 1989, 2005 and 2012 precedents as a bar and not a presentational point?
Can the six B001 supporters agree how the citation should credit Katori's concept and Ye's record-accuracy systems, and is a two-name credit defensible given Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Hinkley?
Should the committee wait for the redefinition of the second, or is demonstrated independent 10^-18 performance sufficient on its own?

Do Danielsson and Eriksson regard B001 as acceptable as the sole prize, and what specific evidence about the pairing mechanism or reproducibility of correlated states would move the B001 supporters to include B017 now?
If B017 is considered, how should the committee record the omission of Cao and other moire-device groups, and does the group-leader convention hold for this experiment?
Is a one-name IceCube credit for Halzen defensible, can it be widened within the credited list, and should the case rest on the diffuse flux alone or on the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 associations?
Should the committee consider a clocks-only prize, a B001 plus B027 prize, or a B001 plus B017 prize, and does adding a second part dilute or strengthen the B001 support?
Should any recusal or discounting follow from the disclosed flags, namely Kroll's Hall-laboratory link on B001, the chair's astroparticle proximity on B027 and Johansson's WACQT proximity on B003?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one centre of gravity: six of eight members explicitly prefer B001 with the same two-name credit, and no member disputes the underlying science. B017 has two explicit supporters and is the most frequent alternative (Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce). B027 rests on one supporter, who himself calls the one-name credit exposed. The open issues are the weight of the 1989, 2005 and 2012 precedents, the maturity of B017, whether a second part is warranted at all, and attribution gaps on every shortlisted candidate. This summary counts only positions stated in the eight files.
